objects.original: One approximate-proximal two-layer Picard phase: exact proximal comparison p, actual stopped map q, successful test count N+1, two refresh Gaussians, two fresh Gaussian arrays, explicit phase map Phi and transition kernel K.
objects.reconstructed: The same p,q,N, driving product law gamma, first and second gradient blocks and both momentum refreshments, with run denoting the exact-real proximalQuery interpreter.
objects.evidence: Algorithm 3.1 steps 1-4 agree term by term after replacing the exact estimator by the Appendix D.1 approximate estimator. The live module uses ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery; the decoder accurately describes that definition, including return of the current iterate and the final counted gradient evaluation.

domains.original: The pinned component accepts a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, a finite deterministic index set, nonnegative h and arbitrary finite real node/weight arrays. The source algorithm itself uses Euclidean phase space, J>=2 and its Chebyshev-Lobatto arrays.
domains.reconstructed: Complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel E; any finite index type I; h>=0; t,omega,b,d arbitrary deterministic real arrays.
domains.evidence: The Lean typeclasses exactly encode the component domain. Euclidean-space transport to finite-dimensional inner-product E is an explicit coordinate-free elaboration; empty/singleton I and h=0 are permitted by the component, and no claim is made that these cases instantiate the paper quadrature. The candidate assumptions state the domain difference and keep the source adapter open.

quantifiers.original: For fixed normalized C2 V, eta,c,eps and supplied arrays, construct common measurable witnesses p,q,N valid at every queried center and a kernel valid at every incoming state.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every admissible space,potential,parameters and arrays, there exist p,q,N with forall y execution/accuracy certificates, followed by an existential K with forall s exact law.
quantifiers.evidence: The phase theorem obtains p,N and defines q before constructing Phi. Both layers use the identical q. The certificates hold for all y, including random centers; the driving law is a constant kernel independent of the incoming state. No realization-dependent existential oracle replaces the common measurable map.

assumptions.original: C2 normalized Hessian bounds kappa^(-1)I<=Hessian V<=I with kappa>=1, 0<eta<=c<1, eps>0, h>=0; finite supplied arrays.
assumptions.reconstructed: The same quadratic-form Hessian inequalities at every x,v; the same parameter inequalities and finite-array conditions.
assumptions.evidence: The source normalization is in Section 3 and Algorithm D.2 assumes precisely 0<eta<=c0<1. Positivity eps>0 is needed for finite stopping; D.1 allows zero accuracy abstractly but D.2 does not. No D.1 stability step-size restriction or repeated-run parameter choice is needed for this kernel existence component, and none is assumed or claimed.

conclusion.original: A measurable stopped query with eps accuracy and successful finite interpreter count, and a jointly measurable explicit update whose independent Gaussian pushforward is a Markov transition law.
conclusion.reconstructed: Measurable p,q,N; exact proximal optimality equation, eps norm error and run success with N+1 fuel/count; nonnegative refresh variance, measurable Phi and Markov K with K(s)=Phi(s,.)_*gamma.
conclusion.evidence: The parent establishes that p is the unique minimizer of V(x)+(2 eta)^(-1)||x-y||^2, so the phase optimality equation legitimately identifies the exact proximal comparison. The probability-kernel statement is a Samplinglib measure-theoretic elaboration, expressly attributed as such; it does not assert a source convergence theorem. The decoder event-law reformulation follows from measurable pushforward.

scopes.original: One coefficient-parametric implemented phase only; source coefficient construction, repeated history, error, invariant law and expected run cost remain separate.
scopes.reconstructed: One explicit transition law and pointwise finite proximal execution/accuracy; no invariant-distribution, convergence, bias or uniform query-complexity conclusion.
scopes.evidence: The live module introduction, candidate assumptions, obligations and lesson all state the finite-array interface boundary. To instantiate Algorithm 3.1 one must separately construct its nodes, omega_ij and terminal weights b_j=omega_{J,j}, d_j=omega_j. This result alone proves neither that adapter nor Algorithm 3.2, Lemma D.1 stability, Lemma D.4 expected work or the main sampling theorems. The lesson makes these boundaries visible.

constant_dependencies.original: The stopped maps depend on V,eta,c,eps; phase law also depends on h and all supplied arrays. a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)); no hidden accuracy or work constant is exported.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same fixed witnesses and parameterized exact law; no asymptotic constant or universal cost bound.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The proof uses eta<1 via eta<=c<1 and the parent pointwise stopping construction. Its auxiliary logarithmic certificate depends on c, but the phase theorem exports only successful count N+1 and accuracy, not a cost bound. Gaussian standard covariance is fixed by stdGaussian; finite product factors supply independence without constants.

deltas.detail: The attributed component generalizes the source Euclidean domain to finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel spaces and allows arbitrary finite index types and h=0. These are disclosed scope extensions of kernel existence, not claims that every input realizes the source numerical scheme.

The deterministic coefficient adapter remains unproved here. The source instantiation requires t_j and weights from (3.6), with positionWeight_j=omega_{J,j} and momentumWeight_j=omega_j. The publication explicitly retains this obligation.

Joint measurability and the explicit probability-kernel construction are Samplinglib additions to the implementation component. They preserve the source update formulas without promoting the source convergence or complexity results.
